title: The Choir of the Weeping Wood
premise: Astrid Ishikawa has spent her nineteen years in the Weeping Wood, a valley where magic cannot enter, tending the last embers of the Emberwrights—a guild that once bound dragon-fire to human souls. When she finds tonight's date inscribed in a century-old prophecy, she learns her guildmaster sold his own soul to the court beneath the mountain to keep the valley hidden, and that the last dragon's flame will gutter out within a season unless that soul is reclaimed. Astrid must leave the only home she's known, bargain with the mountain court's beautiful, treacherous regent, and choose between exposing the guild's founding lie or preserving the loyalty that holds her people together. In the end she reclaims the soul at the cost of her own memories of the valley, returning as a stranger who carries the truth—and the rekindled fire—home.
about_author: Wendell Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing guild ledgers in northern mining towns before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about small communities keeping dangerous secrets, and live somewhere with too many birch trees.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't Supposed to Exist
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. While cataloguing the guild's crumbling archive, Astrid finds a prophecy ledger with tonight's date inked a century ago beside her own name. Her guildmaster Halvard dismisses it, but his hands shake. Emotional beat: quiet dread—the first crack in the safe, unchanging world.

chapters.title: What the Valley Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She tests the valley's boundary and watches magic die at the tree line; beyond it, the last dragon Serevain smolders on the mountain like a dying lamp. Halvard confesses fragments: a debt owed beneath the mountain, due now. Emotional beat: grief for an innocence already lost.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Ledger
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, with a flashback in Halvard's voice via his journal. She discovers he sold his own soul to the mountain court decades ago to seal the valley, buying the guild time—but the price comes due tonight. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with pity; loyalty begins to feel like a cage.

chapters.title: Crossing the Tree Line
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She slips past the ward at dawn, and magic floods into her for the first time—ecstatic and terrifying. The wood itself weeps resin that records memories, showing her glimpses of the guild's true founding. Emotional beat: vertigo and wonder; the world is larger than her loyalties.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Descending through Serevain's hollow, she reaches the glass-lit court of the regent Veyra, who keeps souls as chandeliers. Halvard's soul hangs among them, dimming. Veyra offers a trade: another soul in its place. Emotional beat: seduction and horror; power here is beautiful and rotten.

chapters.title: A Soul for a Soul
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Astrid below, her friend Tomas above discovering what she's done and following. Astrid nearly trades her own soul before learning Veyra cannot release any soul freely—the court feeds on them. Emotional beat: despair sharpening into resolve; bargains are traps.

chapters.title: The Founding Lie
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Following Astrid's trail, he uncovers in the weeping-wood resin that the guild didn't flee magic—they stole it, and the valley's ward runs on stolen dragon-fire and enslaved souls. Emotional beat: disillusionment; the loyalty he cherished was built on a crime.

chapters.title: Serevain's Bargain
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She climbs to the guttering dragon, who reveals the prophecy named her because only someone raised outside magic can carry fire without burning. Serevain offers her the last flame—if she accepts that it will consume her memories of the valley. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh; truth costs everything memory holds dear.

chapters.title: The Chandelier Breaking
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. Carrying dragon-fire, Astrid returns to the court, shatters the soul-chandeliers, and confronts Veyra, who offers her Halvard's throne instead of freedom. Astrid refuses, frees the souls including Halvard's, and escapes as the mountain convulses—with Tomas holding the way open. Emotional beat: sacrifice triumphant, but not clean.

chapters.title: Stranger in the Weeping Wood
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She returns with the fire that will sustain the guild honestly and the freed souls finding rest—but she remembers nothing of the valley or its people, reading her own name in the ledger like a stranger's. Tomas chooses to tell her the truth anyway. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; truth outlasts even lost memory, and belonging can be rebuilt.
